title: Query, subset, intersect, and export genome browser track data

sources.locator: Table Browser Overview; Guided Walkthrough steps 1–6; Optional: filter, subset, or combine tracks
Tutorials overview and Table Browser entry

scientific_use: Select a genome assembly, track/table and genomic region or identifier set; filter rows or intersect with another track; export annotations, selected joined fields, or DNA/protein sequence. A query can answer overlap questions such as which variants fall in coding exons or which regions overlap peaks.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial describes operating the existing UCSC Table Browser service and selecting existing tracks, filters, intersections, and export formats; it does not implement those algorithms.
inputs: Chosen species/genome assembly, track and table, region or identifier list; optional row predicates and second track for overlap/intersection. Track data come from the hosted browser database or user-uploaded lists.
outputs: Queried rows, selected/joined fields, BED/GTF/custom-track records, or sequence in a chosen output format; optional summary statistics such as record count, base coverage, and item-size ranges.
dependencies: UCSC Table Browser web service and availability of the selected assembly/track/table; query size limits vary by track, and whole-genome output may be unavailable.
evidence: Tutorial step 4 documents coordinates, gene lookup, multiple regions, and ID lists; optional section documents filter and intersection semantics; step 5 names formats and sequence export; step 6 names summaries.
limitations: No particular track, assembly, study dataset, or exported artifact was selected in the tutorial, so dataset_ids are empty. A task author must fix the assembly/table snapshot and define expected output and reproducible access; live service state can change.

title: Extract genome sequence from 2bit by sequence, interval list, or BED

sources.locator: usage(); options table; twoBitAndBedToSeq(); processSeqsFromBed(); twoBitToFa()

scientific_use: Retrieve genomic DNA as FASTA for a whole genome, named sequence, half-open zero-based interval, sequence-spec list, or BED-defined regions. BED blocks concatenate exon blocks while excluding introns; negative-strand BED records are reverse-complemented. The optional noMask mode uppercases sequence.
tool_role_basis: The C source implements an existing sequence extraction operation over 2bit reference assets; a task using the command would supply a reference and regions rather than implement sequence extraction itself.
inputs: UCSC .2bit genome assembly (local path or URL); optional sequence name and [start,end), sequence-spec list, or BED coordinates with optional blocks and strand.
outputs: FASTA records for requested genomic sequence; BED-block entries yield concatenated spliced sequence and negative strand entries are reverse-complemented.
dependencies: Compiled kent twoBitToFa binary and readable 2bit input; BED inputs must be compatible with assembly chromosome names and coordinates. Remote access can use UDC cache directory.
evidence: usage() gives half-open zero-based coordinates, flags, BED semantics, URL input and an hg38 example URL; twoBitAndBedToSeq() concatenates blocks and reverse-complements negative strand; twoBitToFa() chooses interval/list/BED extraction.
limitations: The source names hg38.2bit at a moving 'latest' URL but does not pin a file release, size, checksum, or redistribution terms. The extraction code was read, not built or run. BED coordinate and name compatibility must be supplied.

title: Filter VCF records and alternate alleles by position or allele count
scientific_use: Remove variant positions present in an exclusion VCF, remove alternate alleles with fewer than a chosen number of observations, update AC/AN and genotype codes when genotypes are present, and optionally rename IDs from REF/POS/ALT. This supports reproducible allele-count and position filtering of cohort VCFs.
tool_role_basis: The utility applies existing VCF filtering operations to input records; source implementation clarifies semantics but the described task need not create the underlying filtering tool.
inputs: VCF file with CHROM/POS/ID/REF/ALT/QUAL/FILTER/INFO; optional genotype columns, -minAc threshold, and an exclusion VCF whose CHROM/POS values match the primary VCF.
outputs: VCF written to stdout, retaining records/alleles under filters and updating INFO counts and genotypes when applicable; optional IDs are comma-separated REF+POS+ALT labels.
dependencies: Compiled kent vcfFilter binary. If genotypes exist, the implementation trusts and recounts genotypes instead of incoming AC/AN; the source's position hash stores indices per chromosome.
evidence: usage() documents -excludeVcf, -minAc and -rename semantics; vcfFilter() applies filtering and emits VCF; test makefile shows test fixture cases for genotyped and genotype-free input, allele thresholds, rename, and excluded positions; fixture header names NC_045512v2 and source faToVcf.
limitations: The included subset.vcf is a test fixture, not established as a representative released cohort. Its header identifies a reference and sample labels but no study accession, full source FASTA, or licensing terms. Test makefile was inspected; tests were not run.

title: Construct chain files and transfer annotations between assemblies

sources.locator: General guidelines; Same organism lifts; Other organism lifts; sections I–II

scientific_use: Build assembly-to-assembly chains from whole-genome alignments and use chains to map annotations to a newer assembly. The documented same-species example splits the query assembly, aligns query to target with BLAT, then chains, nets, and extracts single-coverage chains; a separate section describes cross-species homology mapping caveats.
tool_role_basis: The document composes existing genome alignment and chain utilities (faSplit, BLAT, axtChain, chainNet, chainNetSubset) into a biological coordinate-transfer workflow.
inputs: Old/target and new/query assembly FASTA plus compatible BLAT/chain/net tools and working storage; annotations to transfer are not specified in the inspected workflow excerpt.
outputs: Assembly-pair .over.chain file and transferred annotation tracks/tables associated with the new assembly; unmapped/split outputs are not fully described in inspected source.
dependencies: Kent suite utilities and historical cluster filesystem/cluster BLAT steps, assembly build-area conventions and chain files. Same-species mapping is said to work best for relatively close assemblies; cross-species chains alone are stated inadequate for homology mapping.
evidence: Document names chain/net commands, directionality (new/query against old/target), output naming conventions and caveats; header explicitly says these instructions are not tested yet and should be run one at a time with checks.
limitations: Workflow is historical and explicitly marked untested; paths and cluster commands are environment-specific. Assembly accessions, concrete annotation set, success rates, handling of unmapped records, and deterministic grading contract are absent. Cross-species use requires other tools and human intervention per document.

title: Project genomic variants to transcript, coding, and protein HGVS descriptions
scientific_use: For each alternate allele in an input VCF, find overlapping transcript alignments and emit genomic, transcript, coding and protein HGVS expressions where necessary reference transcript/CDS/protein data exist. Tests include named variant examples and patch-sequence cases.
tool_role_basis: The command annotates supplied variants against an existing UCSC assembly/transcript database using existing projection/HGVS libraries; the task supported is application of the annotation operation.
inputs: Genome database name, VCF variants, assembly chromosome aliases and sequence window, transcript alignments, transcript sequence, CDS definitions, and protein sequence. The tool queries database tables for those resources; one test loads a local test assembly schema/data first.
outputs: Tab-separated output per variant-transcript-allele with five identifying VCF fields plus transcript accession, HGVS.g, HGVS.n, HGVS.c and HGVS.p; protein/coding expressions may be empty where unsupported. Missing transcript sequence yields a comment.
dependencies: Compiled kent vcfToHgvs; UCSC genome database or assembled compatible test schema, RefSeq/GenBank transcript, CDS, protein, PSL/alignment and chromosome/sequence tables; network cache may be used for remote VCF sources.
evidence: usage() defines database/VCF/output arguments; singleAlleleToHgvsOut() generates four HGVS levels; vcfToHgvs() opens VCF, resolves chromosome aliases, queries transcript alignments and obtains sequence/CDS resources; test makefile loads reference tables and compares expected outputs; input VCF header states GRCh37, resource version v1.0.8, source JenniferYen and a named variant-annotation discordance study.
limitations: Test fixtures use legacy GRCh37 and hg38/patched assemblies with a mixture of prepared test database files and built-in database lookups. Tool source flags symbolic alleles as a TODO. Candidate dataset provenance is stronger than the SARS-CoV-2 filtering fixture but still needs terms/source confirmation; no test execution or current database compatibility was assessed.
